evidence: CDIAL 5228 jihvā explicitly gives Assamese zibhā, Bengali jib, Oriya jibha and the Prakrit jīhā / Maithili jīh / Hindi jīh series. Selected eastern affricated dž-/ḍž-/dz- and western jibe forms preserve source consonants and final vowels. Short jī/ji/jiu/jīū and breathy jʰi/jʰiha are interpreted with the h-containing series and retained as regional weakening/glide/breathiness qualifications, not source corrections. Local Indo-Aryan transmission remains unresolved.
